Humanity spends {{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} a year on clinical trials [@industry-clinical-trial-spending-estimate]. Here are the actual enrollment numbers:

## Enrollment Data from ClinicalTrials.gov

### US Trials (Cumulative)

- Phase 1: 722,619 people (median: 33 per trial)
- Phase 2: 2,181,530 people (median: 60 per trial)
- Phase 3: 6,548,474 people (median: 237 per trial)
- Phase 4: 2,718,541 people (median: 90 per trial)
- **Total: 12.2 million people** across all active/recruiting/completed US trials

But that's cumulative - trials running over many years. To get annual enrollment, divide by average trial duration (~2.7 years):

That's the old estimate based on average trial duration. But we can do better.

![A visualization of US clinical trial enrollment showing the distribution of 12.2 million participants across trial phases 1 through 4, including median participants per trial.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-us-trials-cumulative-bw-academic.jpg)


## The Better Method: Count Completed Trials

We analyzed trials that **actually completed** each year (not estimates):

**US Interventional Trials (Phase 1-4 drug trials only):**

- 2024: 1.66M participants (3,038 completed trials)
- 2023: 1.56M participants (3,557 completed trials)
- 2022: 1.52M participants (3,631 completed trials)
- 2021: 842K participants (3,601 trials)
- 2020: 951K participants (3,366 trials)

**Average US: ~1.5 million/year** (interventional drug trials)

The US represents 54% of the global trials market [@us-clinical-trials-market-2024], so:

**Global: ~2.8 million participants/year** (strict definition - interventional only)

But this excludes observational studies, device trials, and behavioral interventions. If you count everything:

**Global: ~5-8 million participants/year** (all clinical research)

England's data confirms the scale: 1.05 million participants in 2023/24 [@england-trial-participants-2023-24] across all study types.

![A visualization showing the growth of US clinical trial participants from 2020 to 2024 and the comparative scale of global research markets.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-better-method-count-completed-trials-bw-academic.jpg)


## Industry Standard: IQVIA 2022

The most authoritative source is IQVIA's 2022 report [@global-trial-participant-capacity], showing:

**Global: 1.9 million participants annually (2022)**

This represents post-COVID normalization from the 4 million peak in 2021 (when COVID trials dominated). IQVIA tracks actual pharmaceutical industry data, making it more reliable than our ClinicalTrials.gov extrapolations.

![Comparison of global clinical trial participant estimates for 2022, contrasting IQVIA's industry-focused data with broader ClinicalTrials.gov extrapolations.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-industry-standard-iqvia-2022-bw-academic.jpg)


**Why the discrepancy with our 2.8M estimate?**

- IQVIA counts actual industry trials (interventional drug studies)
- Our ClinicalTrials.gov analysis includes government/academic trials
- Different completion date definitions
- Our US-to-global scaling may overestimate

**For our economic model, we use IQVIA's 1.9M** as the conservative baseline for current global trial capacity.

## The Tragedy in Numbers

![A funnel infographic illustrating the massive attrition from 2.4 billion chronic disease patients to the 1.08 billion willing to participate and the mere 1.9 to 5 million who actually enroll in clinical trials annually.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-tragedy-in-numbers-bw-academic.jpg)


Chronic disease patients globally: {{< var current_disease_patients_global >}}

Willing to participate in trials: {{< var willing_trial_participants_global >}} ({{< var patient_willingness_trial_participation_pct >}})

Clinical trial participants annually: **{{< var current_trial_slots_available >}}** (interventional drug trials, IQVIA 2022)

Or **~5 million** if counting all clinical research (observational, device, behavioral)

### Among those who could benefit and are willing to help:

Using the conservative IQVIA figure ({{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} ÷ {{< var willing_trial_participants_global >}} = 0.18%), your odds of actually getting into a drug trial are **1 in 566**.

Even if you count all clinical research (5M ÷ {{< var willing_trial_participants_global >}} = 0.46%), your odds are only **1 in 215**.

Meanwhile, {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily >}} people die every day from diseases we're studying.


![An enrollment funnel illustrating the massive gap between the 2.4 billion people with chronic diseases, the 1.08 billion willing to participate, and the 1.9 million actually admitted to drug trials.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-tragedy-in-numbers-bw-academic.jpg)

## The Access Lottery

{{< var current_disease_patients_global >}} people are living with chronic diseases [@global-burden-disease-chronic-conditions-2013] right now. That's cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, COPD, mental illness, chronic pain.

![A scale comparison showing the massive population of 2.4 billion people living with chronic diseases versus the tiny sliver of 1.9 million people who gain access to drug trials.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-access-lottery-bw-academic.jpg)


They're alive. They're suffering. And they could potentially benefit from the treatments we're studying.

**The ratio: 1 person gets access to drug trials for every 1,263 living with disease** (using IQVIA's 1.9M).

Even counting all clinical research (5M), it's still only 1 in 480.

## The Willingness Gap

And here's what makes it even more infuriating: surveys show 49-51% of people are willing to participate in clinical trials [@patient-willingness-clinical-trials].

![A comparison showing the massive disparity between the 50% of people willing to participate in clinical trials and the 0.08% who actually gain access, illustrating the 'Willingness Gap'.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-willingness-gap-bw-academic.jpg)


**Half of humanity would say yes if asked.**

But only **{{< var current_patient_participation_rate >}} of disease patients actually get to participate in drug trials** ({{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} ÷ {{< var current_disease_patients_global >}}).

Even counting all clinical research, it's just **0.2%** (5M ÷ {{< var current_disease_patients_global >}}).

That's not a recruitment problem. That's an exclusion problem.

The system isn't failing because people don't want to help find cures. It's failing because:

- Trials only exist at major academic medical centers
- Most people live too far away
- Eligibility criteria exclude 90% of patients
- Enrollment caps fill up instantly

We have {{< var willing_trial_participants_global >}} with chronic disease who are willing and able to participate. We're enrolling {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} in drug trials (or ~5M counting all clinical research).

**We're turning away 99.82% of willing participants** (using drug trials), or 99.5% if counting all clinical research.

## The Cost Per Patient

Using IQVIA's {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} drug trial participants:

{{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} ÷ {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} = **$43,684 per participant annually**

Even if we count all clinical research (5M participants):

{{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} ÷ 5 million participants = **$16,600 per participant annually**

That's not per treatment. That's the overhead cost per human enrolled, covering:

- Regulatory paperwork
- Compliance monitoring
- Data collection
- Insurance against lawsuits
- Committees reviewing committees
- The salaries of people whose job is writing protocols

Phase 3 trials (median 237 participants [@clinicaltrials-gov-enrollment-data-2025]) cost {{< var phase_3_trial_cost_min >}} each. That's $84,388 per patient. Not for the drug. For the *trial*.

![A comparison of clinical trial overhead costs per participant relative to the price of a new car, illustrating the high administrative expense per human enrolled.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-cost-per-patient-bw-academic.jpg)


You could buy each participant a new Honda Civic and still have money left over.

## Why This Matters

If you get cancer, your odds of getting into a clinical trial are about 5%. If you're unlucky enough to get a rare disease, your odds of a trial *existing* are basically zero.

![A scale comparison showing the massive gap between the 2.4 billion people suffering from chronic disease and the tiny fraction of 1.9 million patients who participate in drug trials annually.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-why-this-matters-bw-academic.jpg)


The system isn't designed to help sick people try treatments. It's designed to generate data clean enough to satisfy regulators. The fact that some people get treatment is a side effect.

**Humans spend {{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}} a year to help {{< var current_patient_participation_rate >}} of the {{< var current_disease_patients_global >}} people suffering from chronic disease** (using IQVIA's {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} drug trial participants).

Even counting all clinical research, it's just 0.2% (5M participants).

The other 99.92% of disease patients (or 99.82% of willing participants) get to wait. And suffer. And while they wait, {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily >}} die every day.

## What a 1% Treaty Could Do

The math is straightforward:

### Today's Capacity

![A scale comparison visualizing the disparity between global military spending at $2.72 trillion and clinical trials spending at $60 billion, highlighting the magnitude of global resource allocation.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-today-s-capacity-bw-academic.jpg)


- [@global-military-spending]: {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}}
- Clinical trials spending: {{< var global_clinical_trials_spending_annual >}}
- Participants: {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}}/year (drug trials, IQVIA 2022)

#### With 1% of Military Spending Redirected

![A breakdown of the redistribution process showing how 1% of military spending flows into three distinct buckets: VICTORY bonds, IAB incentives, and the remaining majority for clinical trials.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-with-1-of-military-spending-redirected-bw-academic.jpg)


- 1% of {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} = **{{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} treaty funding**
- After VICTORY bonds ({{< var victory_bond_funding_pct >}}) and IAB incentives ({{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}}): **{{< var dih_treasury_trial_subsidies_annual >}} for trials**

#### With Your Decentralized Framework for Drug Assessment

![A visual comparison of a decentralized drug assessment framework versus traditional trial models, highlighting remote enrollment, smartphone reporting, and continuous operation workflows.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-with-your-decentralized-framework-for-drug-assessment-bw-academic.jpg)


- Enrollment isn't limited by proximity to trial sites
- Patients report outcomes via smartphone
- Trials run continuously instead of in isolated batches
- Cost per participant drops to **{{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}}** (pragmatic trial cost, based on RECOVERY trial benchmarks)

#### The Result

- {{< var dih_treasury_trial_subsidies_annual >}} ÷ {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} = **{{< var dih_patients_fundable_annually >}}/year**
- Current: {{< var current_trial_slots_available >}}/year (IQVIA 2022)
- **{{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}× more trial capacity** means testing {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}}× more treatments simultaneously

And we'd only be using a fraction of available capacity ({{< var dih_patients_fundable_annually >}} ÷ {{< var willing_trial_participants_global >}}).

![Comparison of current clinical trial efficiency versus the proposed 1% Treaty model, highlighting the inverse relationship between cost-per-patient and total capacity.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-what-a-1-treaty-could-do-bw-academic.jpg)


The data would be better too. More diverse. More representative. Collected from people living their actual lives instead of visiting clinics every week.

## The Bottom Line

**{{< var current_trial_slots_available >}} people a year (drug trials, IQVIA 2022), at a cost of $43,684 each.**

Or **~5 million** if you count all clinical research (observational, device, behavioral) at **$16,600 each**.

![A scale comparison infographic showing the narrow funnel of clinical research participation, contrasting the 2.4 billion people with chronic diseases against the 5 million in clinical research and 1.9 million in drug trials.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-bottom-line-bw-academic.jpg)


**{{< var current_disease_patients_global >}} people are living with chronic disease.**

### The ratio: 1 in 1,263 (drug trials) or 1 in 480 (all clinical research) among disease patients.

Among willing participants: 1 in 566 (drug trials) or 1 in 215 (all research).

![A visual comparison showing the stark contrast between the total number of diseased patients and the tiny fraction who successfully enroll in drug trials, illustrating the 1 in 1,263 ratio.](/assets/images/clinical-trial-participants/clinical-trial-participants-section-the-ratio-1-in-1-263-drug-trials-or-1-in-480-all-clinical-research-among-disease-patients-bw-academic.jpg)


The 99.92% of disease patients (99.82% of willing participants) who don't get access to drug trials? They suffer. And {{< var global_disease_deaths_daily >}} die every day.
